question.text: <math><mn>0.5</mn></math> moles of gas <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi></math> moles of gas <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> exert a pressure of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>200</mn><mi> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi></math> in a container of volume <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></math> at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1000</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></math> . Given, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></math> is the gas constant in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>JK</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><msup><mi>mol</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi></math> is:

solution.text:
According to the ideal gas equation:

PV=nRT

200×10=(0.5+x)R×1000

2=0.5R+xR

x=2-0.5RR=4-R2R
